evaluation_target.rationale: The hazard defines the unwanted operational event as the vehicle suddenly stopping with no obstacle in front, and SG-3 states the system shall prevent unintended braking.

phenomenon_of_interest.statement: Vehicle braking behavior in the stated urban driving situation, including whether braking occurs without a forward obstacle present.
phenomenon_of_interest.scope: Straight ahead drive on a less frequented urban road at 50 km/h, in good weather, with no visible obstacles or vehicles in front of the ego vehicle.
phenomenon_of_interest.rationale: The hazard specifies the operational situation and the hazardous event that characterizes the relevant braking phenomenon to be evaluated.

distinctions.dimension: Presence of a forward obstacle relevant to braking
distinctions.contrast_a: A forward obstacle is present in front of the ego vehicle in the operational situation.
distinctions.contrast_b: No forward obstacle is present in front of the ego vehicle in the operational situation.
distinctions.rationale: The hazardous event explicitly contrasts braking with no obstacle in front; collapsing these cases would remove the information needed to evaluate whether braking is unintended versus a collision-avoidance response.
The safety goal concerns unintended braking itself, so distinguishing braking from non-braking is necessary to evaluate whether the hazard occurs.

orrs.obligation: An admissible observable representation shall preserve whether braking occurs and whether a forward obstacle is present in the declared operational situation.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must allow the cases 'braking with no forward obstacle' and 'no braking' to remain distinguishable, and must also distinguish braking with a forward obstacle from braking with no forward obstacle.

orrs.obligation: An admissible observable representation shall preserve whether an obstacle is present in front of the ego vehicle when braking behavior is evaluated.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must not collapse obstacle-present and obstacle-absent forward scene states into the same representation when assessing braking behavior.
